title: Managing Static IP Address - Using NMTUI
description: Configure and validate a static IPv4 address on a Linux system using NetworkManager.

lab_objective.description: In this lab, students will learn how to configure a static IP address using NetworkManager's text-based interface, understand IPv4 addressing concepts such as IP address and prefix, configure a gateway and DNS servers, activate the connection, and validate network connectivity step by step.
objectives: Understand what nmtui is and how it is used to manage NetworkManager connections.
Identify the current network configuration using nmcli dev show.
Configure a static IPv4 address using nmtui.
Understand the difference between an IP address, prefix, gateway, and DNS server.
Configure a default gateway and DNS servers.
Enable automatic connection for the network profile.
Validate the IP address, routing table, NetworkManager status, and connection profile.
Test network connectivity in a layered troubleshooting approach.
Differentiate between connectivity problems and DNS resolution problems.
scenario: You are a Linux administrator responsible for configuring networking on a Linux VM. The VM currently has a NetworkManager connection, and you need to configure a static IPv4 address instead of relying on DHCP. You must first identify the current network configuration and then configure the static IP address, prefix, gateway, and DNS servers. After making the changes, activate the connection and validate the configuration. Finally, test connectivity from the local interface to the gateway, then to an external IP address, and finally test DNS name resolution.
Configure Networking Using nmtui (NetworkManager Text User Interface) to configure a static IPv4 address.

Never casually bring down the interface carrying your current remote SSH session.

steps: You should see the same IP address like inet 192.168.111.xxx/24
expected - Look for something similar to default via 192.168.111.1 dev ens192

tasks.title: Test Connectivity
steps: Testing should be done in layers.
Instead, troubleshoot from the inside outward.
Confirm that the expected IP exists.
The VM can reach its gateway.
If this fails, do not immediately blame DNS. DNS has not even been tested yet. So fix gateway
If this works but 'ping google.com' fails, the problem may be DNS.
If name resolution works, DNS is probably functioning.

completion_message: You have successfully configured a static IP address using nmtui, activated the NetworkManager connection, validated the IP configuration and routing, and tested connectivity from the local interface through the gateway, external IP, and DNS resolution.
